unresolved_notes.printed: \mathfrak X_{(\hat x)} in the supplied source layers
unresolved_notes.decision: Keep the supplied source-layer hat reading; do not invent a further glyph correction.
unresolved_notes.reason: The two current source pages both use the completion hat and the same completion-to-localization isomorphism. The earlier convention entry questioned the physical overstrike; without the scan that paleographic question cannot be independently resolved. The authoritative attached layers remain the printed-reading witness.

unresolved_notes.decision: Retain the printed blank reference in every body; record the suggested reference only as a note.
unresolved_notes.reason: The statement lacks a number in the recorded print. More than one preceding smoothness result could support the argument, and adding 4.13(a) would manufacture a citation. No supplied source establishes the omitted numeral.

unresolved_notes.printed: Attached layers use separate paragraphs after numbered headings
unresolved_notes.alternative: possible printed run-in headings with following prose on the same paragraph
unresolved_notes.decision: Keep the supplied paragraph boundaries; do not make an unchecked global reflow.
unresolved_notes.reason: The two specific changes were held at low confidence and the other headings were not verified. A text-only layer cannot establish a printed indentation or run-in break. This is a layout uncertainty, not grounds for altering any authorial wording.

unresolved_notes.decision: Retain E in all bodies; record the proposed X reading without adopting it.
unresolved_notes.reason: The preceding concrete extension is called X, but the transitivity isomorphism is valid for any extension E. Consequently the typography does not force a mathematical error. Both supplied layers retain E, and an authorial generic E remains possible.

unresolved_notes.decision: Retain the source-layer lowercase psi in the body.
unresolved_notes.reason: The footnote names a category also denoted by underlined capital Psi in the main text, but the recorded low-confidence observation does not establish whether the glyph is a typist variant or an accidental change. No scan is supplied to adjudicate its shape.

unresolved_notes.alternative: second display (3.2.3\prime) or another new tag
unresolved_notes.decision: Retain both printed (3.2.3) tags; distinguish their locations by description in the records.
unresolved_notes.reason: The following source already uses (3.2.4); no unoccupied intended number is established. An editorial prime would be a new citation system, not recovery of the author’s number. The diagram and c(X,alpha) display remain distinguishable by their content.

unresolved_notes.alternative: a possible printed dot below the opening parenthesis
unresolved_notes.decision: Keep the supplied formula without an additional dot.
unresolved_notes.reason: No mathematical operation is defined by the possible mark. Its status as ink, damage or punctuation is a visual-source question; neither attached layer encodes it.

unresolved_notes.decision: Retain the attached diplomatic reading extension, and list the alternative only in the note.
unresolved_notes.reason: The two source layers agree. The earlier candidate was explicitly held and supplies no established printed lexical error. The scan is needed to distinguish an actual o from a damaged e and a line-end hyphen.

unresolved_notes.alternative: a proposed replacement pencil with an isolated ordinary quadratic singularity
unresolved_notes.decision: Preserve the supplied mathematical formula; do not construct a new proof or pencil.
unresolved_notes.reason: The global record explicitly calls the proposed replacement a repair of the mathematics rather than a recovered reading. The detailed proposed formula is not supplied in the attached findings file. The recorded concern (a singular plane for n=2k+1 at least 7) is disclosed, but no conjectural replacement is inserted.

unresolved_notes.printed: source-layer continuous underlines through some inner commas
unresolved_notes.alternative: stop and restart each underline around the comma
unresolved_notes.decision: Keep the source-layer markup pending visual evidence at each occurrence.
unresolved_notes.reason: The global record states that the typist sometimes underlined through commas and sometimes did not. Therefore a string-wide rule is not justified; each of the potential cases requires its scan. No authorial wording is changed.

unresolved_notes.decision: Keep the comma as argument punctuation; do not move it into the subscript.
unresolved_notes.reason: The lower comma was a held visual observation, not a new index. The H_s followed by coefficient argument consistently denotes the fibre. Both layers retain ordinary argument punctuation; a physical baseline question requires the scan.

unresolved_notes.decision: Retain oh miracle as the attached diplomatic reading.
unresolved_notes.reason: The later supplied layers agree on oh. The earlier low-confidence record does not establish the visual reading independently; changing both layers back to ô would discard the current witness without evidence.

unresolved_notes.alternative: a slash presentation of the same quotient
unresolved_notes.decision: Keep the displayed fraction in both layers.
unresolved_notes.reason: Both attached layers encode the same numerator and denominator as a quotient. The proposed slash concerns the original graphic layout alone. No mathematical change follows, and without a scan the alternative typography cannot be established.

unresolved_notes.decision: Keep the attached diplomatic subseteq reading.
unresolved_notes.reason: The issue reports a possible overstrike, not a verified symbol. Historical subset notation may also be non-strict, so semantics do not settle the physical stroke. No inequality is silently modernized.

unresolved_notes.printed: \Delta_B throughout the defining discussion; \Lambda_B in printed (5.0.12)
unresolved_notes.alternative: change all seven \Delta_B to \Lambda_B, or retain current \Delta_B at (5.0.12)
unresolved_notes.decision: Keep the supplied diplomatic glyphs and the local current Delta correction; reject an unchecked all-seven replacement.

The earlier global all-seven proposal requires scans of all occurrences and cannot override the later source-layer distinction. The physical glyph family remains a scan question.

unresolved_notes.alternative: \Psi_q suggested by the typewriter capital-form glyph
unresolved_notes.decision: Retain psi consistently with the attached source notation; do not recase the operator.
unresolved_notes.reason: Issue 78 excludes glyph-only substitutions from textual diplomatic variants. The operator is the same Dwork operator defined earlier in Exposé XXII; its cap-height typescript form does not introduce a second operator. No scan-backed case distinction is available.

unresolved_notes.printed: source underlines sometimes include mathematical symbols and final punctuation
unresolved_notes.alternative: split each underline around symbols and punctuation according to the print
unresolved_notes.decision: Retain the supplied markup except for exact separately documented repairs, including ED-XV-1.3.2-i.
unresolved_notes.reason: The global record defers these cases to the individual visual review required by issue 48; the typist did not follow one mechanically inferable rule. A broad replacement would silently modify authorial presentation at unverified loci.
